citations.locator: EcoCrop_DB.csv row for ScientificName="Solanum melongena"; field TMAX
citations.note: TMAX is ECOCROP's stated absolute upper bound of 'the full range of temperatures under which the plant will grow' (full adaptability range), not a stated daily-maximum air-temperature damage onset. The ECOCROP tutorial (.research-sources/2026-11-06/ecocrop-tutorial.pdf, p.2) defines TOPMN/TOPMX as 'the optimal growing temperature adaptability range (the range of temperatures under which the plant will grow optimally)' and TMIN/TMAX as part of 'the full growing temperature adaptability range (the full range of temperatures under which the plant will grow)... All entries are absolute values.' Neither definition states a daily-maximum or daily-minimum air-temperature basis, a duration, or a growth stage; ECOCROP's underlying climate matching (Hijmans et al.) compares these to long-run mean monthly temperatures, not single-day extremes. TMIN/TMAX are therefore NOT used here as whole-cycle damage limits outright; they are recorded as the closest FAO-tier evidence with this basis gap explicit in missingFields. The builder could not re-find the quote in the saved text, so it is not reproduced.

references.summary: Warm-season fruiting vegetable with a prolonged harvest period. Chilling restricts growth and frost damages plants. Excessive heat and water stress can impair flower retention and fruit set. Tomato, pepper and potato may share some diseases; host specificity still needs organism-level checking. Transplant age and the distinction between first picking and final picking affect the cycle definition.
